title: Dynamic Slab Batcher with Prefetch and KV Coalescing for Streaming Chat
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Problem: Streaming chat workloads produce many short, interleaved single-token continuations. Naive batching either wastes GPU memory by reserving large KV slabs per stream or inflates latency by waiting for large batches. We need a batch formation heuristic that simultaneously minimizes per-token latency, bounds peak GPU memory, and maximizes amortized kernel throughput for multi-turn chat with prefix reuse.
implementation_notes: High-level approach: 1) Dynamic slab allocator: maintain a small number of slab sizes (32, 128, 512 token capacity) and assign incoming streams to the smallest slab that fits current suffix + anticipated growth. 2) Probabilistic prefetch: for streams that historically extend beyond 1 token (based on user/session model), prefetch KV into a shared slab window to avoid cold-cache penalties. 3) KV coalescing: detect near-identical prefixes across streams (exact or fuzzy by hashing first N tokens) and share KV pages rather than duplicating. 4) Early flush window: when low-latency SLOs are at risk, flush partially-filled batches after a short watermark (e.g., 6ms) rather than waiting for full slab occupancy. 5) Preemption policy: high-priority interactive streams can preempt low-priority background batches by stealing a slot from the smallest slab and triggering a micro-batch flush. 6) Memory compaction pass: periodically (low-traffic window) compact underutilized slabs to defragment GPU memory, moving cold KV to a quantized CPU-backed staging area if needed.
heuristics_detail:
- Sequence-length bucketing: group streams by current active token-length and remaining cold-prefix length to choose kernel path and slab.
- Size estimate: use LRU-length estimator per session to predict next-k tokens with exponential moving average (alpha=0.2).
- Coalesce threshold: if two streams share >=80% of the first 64 tokens (or identical prompt hash) and both have compatible position encodings, map them to shared KV references.
- Prefetch budget: cap prefetch total memory to 12% of GPU memory per device to avoid eviction storms.
- Watermark policy: dynamically adapt watermark from 6ms to 40ms based on observed p95 latency vs SLO.
- Fallback: if slab allocation would exceed reserved GPU slab pool, fall back to streaming kernel with CPU-backed KV shards (quantized) to preserve latency at cost of throughput.
performance_targets:
- P50 token latency <= 18ms for short-turn (<16 tokens) interactive streams on T4-equivalent.
- P95 token latency <= 90ms under 70% cluster utilization.
- Reduce per-stream peak KV memory by 25% on average compared to naive per-stream allocation.
- Increase average tokens/sec per GPU by 18% for chat workloads with high prefix reuse.
acceptance_criteria: Implements slab allocator with 3 slab sizes and correct eviction semantics
KV coalescing avoids duplicate KV pages for identical prefixes (validated by memory diffs)
Prefetch budget respected under synthetic high-growth session tests
Bench results meet P50/P95 targets in controlled canary (internal perf-suite)
Rollout playbook and metrics dashboard created in Console with cost/latency breakouts
qa_plan: Unit tests for slab allocation and eviction corner cases
Integration test: 1k concurrent short-turn chat sessions with random prefix collisions
Chaos test: force GPU OOM path and verify graceful fallback to quantized CPU path
Canary: deploy to 5% of requests for a subset of regions with close monitoring
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect KV coalescing may produce wrong position encodings or stale attention caches. Mitigation: strict validation step that verifies identical attention scores on small reference prompts before enabling coalescing for a prefix group. Risk: compaction moves KV while kernels hold references -> potential races. Mitigation: use epoch-based GC and double-buffering during compaction with telemetry to detect refcount mismatch.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag and per-customer opt-in. 2) Internal canary with non-critical workloads (5%). 3) Expand to low-traffic orgs (20%) after 48h and no regressions. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% with telemetry-driven rollback thresholds (p95 latency increase > 10% or error rate spike).
